evals.name: url-happy-path
evals.expected_output: A ghostty entry appended to src/content/gallery/index.ts with the repo's own description as the tagline, accurate platforms, a valid category key, the repo's license, and 4-6 features drawn from the README. Its logo downloaded into src/content/gallery/logos/. pnpm build and pnpm lint pass.
assertions: A new entry was appended to the gallery array in src/content/gallery/index.ts with id, name, tagline, category, platforms, upstream and features all populated
The tagline is the upstream repo's own GitHub description, verbatim (not a rewritten or embellished version)
The category is an existing key of CATEGORIES in src/content/gallery/types.ts, or a new key was properly added to types.ts rather than used inline
Every platform listed is a valid PlatformId key and is supported by what the upstream repo actually documents — Windows is not claimed unless the repo documents Windows support
The features list has between 3 and 7 bullets and each one is traceable to the upstream README rather than general knowledge
pnpm build completes successfully
pnpm lint reports no errors
If the entry sets a logo field, a file with exactly that name exists in src/content/gallery/logos/; if it omits logo, no orphan logo file was added
No pre-existing gallery entry was modified or removed — the diff to index.ts is additive

evals.name: name-only-no-icon
evals.prompt: can you add bat to the gallery — the cat clone with syntax highlighting and git integration
evals.expected_output: The name resolved to sharkdp/bat (not a namesake or fork). Entry appended with accurate cross-platform support and a CLI platform tag. The repo has no square app icon, so either a suitable asset is found and justified, or the logo field is omitted so the card falls back to a letter tile — but never a dangling logo reference. pnpm build and pnpm lint pass.
assertions: The ambiguous name 'bat' was resolved to the sharkdp/bat repository, not a fork or unrelated project of the same name
A new entry was appended to the gallery array with id, name, tagline, category, platforms, upstream and features all populated
The tagline is the upstream repo's own GitHub description, verbatim
The platforms list includes 'cli' and reflects bat's actual cross-platform support
The category is an existing key of CATEGORIES, or a new key was properly added to types.ts
pnpm build completes successfully
pnpm lint reports no errors
There is no dangling logo reference: either the logo field is omitted (letter-tile fallback) or the named file exists in src/content/gallery/logos/
The run states where the logo came from, or explains why the logo field was omitted, rather than leaving it unexplained

evals.name: batch-closed-source
evals.prompt: add rectangle and raycast to the gallery
evals.expected_output: Both entries added in one pass with a single batched build. Rectangle resolves to rxhanson/Rectangle. Raycast has no upstream source repo (only raycast/extensions), so the entry should use the homepage as upstream and say so, rather than passing off an unrelated repo as the project's source. pnpm build and pnpm lint pass.
assertions: Two new entries were appended to the gallery array, one for Rectangle and one for Raycast
Rectangle's upstream points at the rxhanson/Rectangle repository
Raycast's entry does not present an unrelated repo (e.g. raycast/extensions) as the application's own source — it either uses the homepage as upstream or explicitly explains what the linked repo is
The report or entry note discloses that Raycast is not open source, rather than implying it is
Each entry's tagline comes from the project's own description rather than being invented
Every platform listed is a valid PlatformId key and matches what each project documents
pnpm build completes successfully
pnpm lint reports no errors
Neither entry has a dangling logo reference: any logo field names a file that exists in src/content/gallery/logos/
The work was batched — metadata gathered for both projects before writing, with a single verification build at the end rather than one build per project
